title: Interleaved row-sampling and query-window smoothing to mitigate dashboard tail latency
creator: Asha Patel
description:
Background: Several customer-facing dashboards have experienced long-tail (>95th percentile) latencies during large tenant queries that request deep pagination ranges or wide time windows. Current mitigation (increasing time-bucketed materialized views and aggressive prefetch) reduces average latency but amplifies tail cases under read-fanout and bursty ingestion patterns.

Goal: Reduce 95th/99th percentile dashboard query latency for tenant queries that page beyond the first few pages and for high-cardinality aggregations, without materially increasing cost or reducing freshness guarantees. We want a deployable, incremental solution that complements the current adaptive-prefetch layer and preserves per-tenant fairness.

Proposed approach: Introduce an interleaved row-sampling proxy at the query-API layer plus a query-window smoothing controller in the query planner. Key ideas: (1) For deep pagination requests we return a deterministic sampled subset of rows (seeded by query fingerprint + tenant id) and expose a lightweight continuation token for client-side progressive fetch. Sampling reduces backend fanout and index range read size while preserving statistical fidelity for most dashboard visualizations. (2) For very wide time windows we dynamically rewrite the query into a multi-window stitched plan where we prioritize hot intervals and return the first response quickly with background stitching for colder intervals. (3) Combine with KV-cache hints to avoid rehydrating large prefix caches for low-priority background intervals.

Design details: - Sampling strategy: stratified reservoir sampling per tenant-window keyed by (metric, time-bucket, tenant). Default sample rate 20% for page > 3, configurable by tenant tier. Samples are deterministic so repeated cursor fetches converge. - Continuation token: short opaque token that encodes sampler state + planner cursors; small enough to be paged by clients. - Window smoothing: planner estimates per-interval selectivity and assigns staging: immediate (hot) vs deferred (cold). Immediate intervals are fully materialized or sampled; deferred intervals are queued for background stitching with lower IO priority. - KV cache integration: when the immediate plan hits a cached prefix, leverage cached aggregates; for deferred intervals do not populate cache unless request frequency crosses threshold.

Metrics and success criteria: - Reduce 95th percentile tail latency for dashboard queries with page > 3 by at least 40% across production tenants. - Reduce the number of backend read shards touched per request by at least 35% for sampled queries. - No more than 5% divergence in common aggregate visualizations (sum/avg/count) vs full-scan baseline for sampled pages. - No regression in first-page latency or in SLAs for dedicated customers.

Milestones: - Spike (1 week): bench different sampling rates on historical query traces, validate fidelity vs dashboard dashboards (PRDs: https://confluence.redwood.ai/display/ENG/ENG-1009999-spike). - Design (1 week): finalize token format, planner rewrite rules, and KV-cache hint protocol. - Implementation (3 weeks): proxy sampler, planner changes, KV-cache hook, unit/integration tests. - Dogfood (2 weeks): enable for internal teams and selected low-tier tenants behind feature flag. - Rollout (2 weeks): staged ramp to all tenants with metrics gating.

Acceptance criteria: - Automated tests for deterministic sampling and continuation tokens. - Bench results uploaded to dashboard: https://dashboards.redwood.ai/query-performance/ENG-1009999. - Rollout feature flag and canary metrics show tail-latency improvement and no increase in error rates. - Documentation updated: Console Query Performance runbook + API changes (Drive: https://drive.redwood.ai/docs/console-query-sampling).

Trade-offs and risks: - Sampling may hide rare outliers and could reduce fidelity for some exploratory flows; mitigation includes ensuring customers can opt-out or request full-scans for ad-hoc queries and surface ‘sampled’ badges in the UI. - Continuation token complexity increases client-side handling; we will provide SDK helpers in the Console SDK and fall back to server-side rehydration for older clients. - Planner estimation errors can misclassify hot intervals; add conservative thresholds and telemetry to tune.

Open questions: - Default sample rate and per-tenant tiers for sampling vs full-scan. - UX for showing sampled results and an easy “full fetch” action. - Cost model and billing implications for staged/background stitching.

Artifacts and links: - Spike notebook & trace replay PR: https://github.com/redwood-inference/console-query-perf/pull/412 - Design doc: https://confluence.redwood.ai/display/ENG/ENG-1009999-design - Benchmark dashboard: https://dashboards.redwood.ai/query-performance/ENG-1009999 - Client SDK helpers issue: https://github.com/redwood-inference/console-sdk/issues/88
comments: 2025-03-01 - Triage: Raised after customer support flagged multiple tenant dashboards with >10s tail during ingestion spikes. Assigned to Jordan Lee for spike.
2025-03-03 - Spike complete: Replay of last 30 days of query traces with deterministic sampling shows 40-55% backend read reduction at 20% sample rate. Notebook: github PR referenced in doc.
2025-03-05 - Design review: PM (Miguel Torres) requested explicit UX flag and opt-out. Design to add a small 'sampled' pill in tables. Linked to PM workstream.

2025-03-07 - Bench warning: For a specific high-cardinality tenant, sampling introduced 8% error on a tail percentile metric; we will add stratified sampling with per-metric thresholds as a mitigation.
2025-03-09 - Implementation kickoff: Proxy sampler module scaffolded, planner rewrite stub merged behind feature flag. PR: https://github.com/redwood-inference/console-query-perf/pull/419
2025-03-10 - Next steps: Complete KV-cache hint hook and end-to-end tests. Plan dogfood rollout to internal analytics team mid-March.
